newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine teachers end protest after riots.
newsitem.headline: Argentine teachers end protest after riots.

text.p: Teachers in an Argentine province shaken by the death of a woman during riots lifted a month-long strike after reaching a deal with government officials late on Saturday, authorities said.
But the national teachers federation CTERA and union grouping CTA ratified calls for a nationwide strike on Monday to denounce police repression.

Teachers and local residents clashed fiercely with security forces early on Saturday in southern Neuquen province, leaving dead a 24-year-old cleaning woman who was on her way to work and injured 13 others.
Teresa Rodriguez, a mother of three children, was hit in the neck by a stray bullet as border guard forces evicted strikers from national highway 2 near the towns of Cutral-Co and Plaza Huincul.
The protestors, whose towns suffer high unemployment, burned tyres and set up barricades along the highway, demanding better wages and working conditions for teachers.

Late in the night the teachers agreed to return to work after reaching a preliminary agreement on wage claims with Gov. Felipe Sapag, who said their protests were infiltrated by "armed ideological groups."
Interior Minister Carlos Corach said Saturday the 32- calibre bullet which killed Rodriguez was not fired by border guard forces or police.
But legislators from opposition parties demanded his resignation over the riots, during which the security forces used tear gas bombs and rubber bullets.
